The current CSV aggregation uses `FMP Area == BSAI`, both pollock target
categories, the single `Scypho jellies` group, and the sum of retained and
discarded `Nontarget Estimate (mt)` records. BSAI includes BS and AI. Annual
BSAI totals reconcile to BS plus AI and to retained plus discarded totals.
The current export contains no exact duplicate rows, and all BSAI jellyfish
weight records are populated. All 2019–2022 BSAI jellyfish detail-record counts
are one, so weighting by that count produces the same totals.

## Source-history finding

The September 10, 2024 assessment source at revision `c29d1e0` contains
jellyfish totals close to the current CSV totals. The November 5 source at
revision `d38de13` approximately doubled the 2019–2022 totals. In 2019 the
November total is exactly twice the September total at stored precision;
other years differ slightly as well as showing the same twofold pattern.
The earlier 2003–2018 jellyfish totals stayed unchanged across these revisions.
The November summary was carried into the 2024 SAFE table.

The factor-of-two pattern therefore predates the current processing and is
already present in the historical summary CSV. The 2024 Quarto table code
reads that precomputed CSV and formats it; it supplies no doubling step.
The upstream raw export or aggregation operation that introduced the larger
historical totals remains unavailable in the inspected record. Duplication
in that upstream preparation is a plausible explanation, not an established
mechanism. The current table retains the directly summed CSV estimates.

## Competing explanations checked

- **Area:** AI contributes only 0.122 t in 2020 and 0.00685 t in 2022, with zero
  in 2019 and 2021. Including all GOA and inside-water records still falls far
  below the 2024 SAFE totals.
- **Species:** Jellyfish are selected directly from the single source group
  `Scypho jellies`; the mapping of other nontarget columns has no effect.
- **Disposition:** Both retained and discarded weights are included once.
  In 2019 all BSAI jellyfish records are discarded. In 2020–2022 the retained
  component is included and is much smaller than the discrepancy.
- **Duplicates/units:** Exact-duplicate rows are absent. The source field is
  already metric tons, and no record-count expansion or unit conversion is applied.

```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(gt)
z <- read_csv("jellyfish-history-audit.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
z |>
  filter(Year >= 2019, Year <= 2022) |>
  select(Year, September2024_mt, November2024_mt, BSAI_mt,
         discarded_mt, retained_mt, November_over_current) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(columns = -Year, decimals = 3) |>
  tab_source_note("All catch values are unrounded annual sums in metric tons; ratios are dimensionless.")
```
